greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Peace be with you as we gather in the presence of the Lord, who dwells among us as our refuge and our strength.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the living temple of God's presence: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the stream that gladdens the city of God: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you raise up the fallen and make all things new: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The waters of the river gladden the city of God, the holy dwelling of the Most High!
homily:
We begin today with a single, quiet image: the threshold. Think of the threshold of your own home. It is the place where the world ends and your sanctuary begins. It is the point of transition where you leave behind the noise, the dust, and the demands of the day, and you step into a space that is yours—a place of rest, of family, and of belonging. In the Book of Ezekiel today, we see a vision of a temple, but it is not a silent, static building. The prophet sees water flowing out from beneath the threshold, a trickle that becomes a river, a torrent that brings life to everything it touches. Wherever this water flows, the desert blooms, the salt is made fresh, and life multiplies. It is an image of God’s grace not staying contained within walls, but spilling out to heal the world.

I want you to hold onto this image: the water flowing from the threshold. It is the image of a life that is so full of the Spirit that it cannot help but overflow. It is the image of the grace that Benjamin Vo carried—a grace that touched everyone who knew him, a grace that continues to ripple outward like that river, bringing life long after the moment of his passing.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been four months since he moved from this life into the fullness of God’s presence. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the brilliant, curious mind that loved to explore the architecture of the world, the gentle, respectful spirit that made him such a treasure to his parents—are suddenly interrupted by the sharp, cold realization that he is not there in the way he once was. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary Tuesday. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. 

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Listen to what Jesus says to those who demand a sign in the temple: 'Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up.' They were looking at stone and mortar, at the forty-six years of human construction. But Jesus was speaking of His own Body. He was speaking of the true temple, the place where God and humanity meet. Benjamin, too, was a temple of the Holy Spirit. Think of that brilliant, searching mind—the way he mastered mathematics, the way he dived into the complexities of cloud infrastructure, or how he coded his own games in his GitHub repository. He loved the logic of systems, the way a problem could be solved if you just worked at it long enough. But think of the gentleness of his spirit, which was the true architecture of his life. Think of the way he loved to look at airplanes, dreaming of his ‘con chim airlines.’ He wasn’t just looking at metal and engines; he was looking at the horizon, looking for the next place to explore, the next connection to be made. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who is now at the banquet of heaven, interceding for you. He is not a memory; he is a living soul, fully alive in the love of God. He has found the destination he was searching for, and he is waiting for the rest of his family to arrive.

Consider the first reading from Ezekiel again: 'Wherever the river flows, every sort of living creature that can multiply shall live.' This is the promise of the Resurrection. The river of God’s love does not stop at the grave. It flows right through it. It makes the salt waters fresh. It turns the bitterness of loss into the sweetness of hope. Benjamin’s life was a tributary of that river. Think of that remarkable moment when he unprompted told his parents that he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for eternity. He was a boy who knew that the true wealth of life is not what we keep, but what we are willing to offer for the sake of those we love. That love is still flowing. It flows in the well dedicated in his name, it flows in the meals shared in his honor, and it flows in the kindness you show to one another every single day.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming.

We hear in the letter to the Corinthians today: 'Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?' This is the turn of the heart. Paul is telling us that our grief is not the end of the story. Our grief is a form of love that is waiting for its reunion. We do not grieve like those who have no hope, because our hope is anchored in the Resurrection. We know that the temple of Benjamin’s life was not destroyed; it was transformed. It was raised up in the glory of the Father’s house. We know that the one who has gone before us is not lost to us; he is simply waiting in the light, where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father.

Think of the dream you had, Alan. You were waiting in line to buy ice cream, and Ben paid. That is the image of the kingdom. It is the image of the one who has gone before us, the one who is now in the position of the steward of grace, waiting to welcome you. He is not distant. He is not gone. He is simply ahead, preparing the way. He is the one who will one day stand at the door of the Father’s house and say, 'I am here, and my family is with me.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was a reminder that the bond you share is not broken by death. It is only changed, deepened, and held in the eternal keeping of God. He is well, he is strong, and he is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected in the sight of God.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, he is waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is the one who has already passed the test, as he said in your dream: 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết.' He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, cheeky grin, looking out toward an endless horizon. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity, holding the key. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in His light, and may the peace of Christ dwell in your hearts forever. Amen.
petition_call: In our need, we turn to the Lord and say:
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all families who carry the weight of grief, that they may be consoled by the promise of the Resurrection and find hope in the love of God, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
The angel brought me

back to the entrance of the temple,

and I saw water flowing out

from beneath the threshold of the temple toward the east,

for the façade of the temple was toward the east;

the water flowed down from the southern side of the temple,

south of the altar.

He led me outside by the north gate,

and around to the outer gate facing the east,

where I saw water trickling from the southern side.

He said to me,

"This water flows into the eastern district down upon the Arabah,

and empties into the sea, the salt waters, which it makes fresh.

Wherever the river flows,

every sort of living creature that can multiply shall live,

and there shall be abundant fish,

for wherever this water comes the sea shall be made fresh.

Along both banks of the river, fruit trees of every kind shall grow;

their leaves shall not fade, nor their fruit fail.

Every month they shall bear fresh fruit,

for they shall be watered by the flow from the sanctuary.

Their fruit shall serve for food, and their leaves for medicine."

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (5) The waters of the river gladden the city of God, the holy dwelling of the Most High!

God is our refuge and our strength,

an ever-present help in distress.

Therefore, we fear not, though the earth be shaken

and mountains plunge into the depths of the sea.

R. The waters of the river gladden the city of God, the holy dwelling of the Most High!

There is a stream whose runlets gladden the city of God,

the holy dwelling of the Most High.

God is in its midst; it shall not be disturbed;

God will help it at the break of dawn.

R. The waters of the river gladden the city of God, the holy dwelling of the Most High!

The LORD of hosts is with us;

our stronghold is the God of Jacob.

Come! behold the deeds of the LORD,

the astounding things he has wrought on earth.

R. The waters of the river gladden the city of God, the holy dwelling of the Most High!

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:

You are God's building.

According to the grace of God given to me,

like a wise master builder I laid a foundation,

and another is building upon it.

But each one must be careful how he builds upon it,

for no one can lay a foundation other than the one that is there,

namely, Jesus Christ.



Do you not know that you are the temple of God,

and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?

If anyone destroys God's temple,

God will destroy that person;

for the temple of God, which you are, is holy.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Since the Passover of the Jews was near,

Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

He found in the temple area those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves,

as well as the money-changers seated there.

He made a whip out of cords

and drove them all out of the temple area, with the sheep and oxen,

and spilled the coins of the money-changers

and overturned their tables,

and to those who sold doves he said,

"Take these out of here,

and stop making my Father's house a marketplace."

His disciples recalled the words of Scripture,

Zeal for your house will consume me.

At this the Jews answered and said to him,

"What sign can you show us for doing this?"

Jesus answered and said to them,

"Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up."

The Jews said,

"This temple has been under construction for forty-six years,

and you will raise it up in three days?"

But he was speaking about the temple of his Body.

Therefore, when he was raised from the dead,

his disciples remembered that he had said this,

and they came to believe the Scripture

and the word Jesus had spoken.

pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there.
